check_substitution_associativity.signature:
pub fn check_substitution_associativity(
    theory: &LawvereTheory,
    cases: &[(&str, usize, &str, usize, &str)],
) -> Vec<String>
check_substitution_associativity.obligation: For each supplied case, checked usize i+j is admitted before lookups; overflow emits exactly one ordered i/j diagnostic and continues. Otherwise compare g[j]h then f[i]result with f[i]g then result[i+j]h. Both defined/equal succeeds; both defined/different emits exact mismatch payload, and either absent emits undefined, including both absent. Preserve all failing-case order/multiplicity. Empty list is vacuous; do not admit arbitrary operations or infer universal associativity.

is_declared_idempotent.obligation: Conjoin actual one-input/one-output shape and the explicit slot-zero own-name/own-name table result equal to the own name. Absence or differing result fails; no mathematical idempotence beyond this raw entry.

Each query makes O(log(S+1)) lexicographic key comparisons, with String comparison byte cost explicit. No temporary owned String lookup keys occur in nested diagnostics.

Associativity uses at most four substitution queries per admitted case, O(S+C log(S+1)) comparison count plus input/result-string lengths and allocation of at most C diagnostic strings. Cauchy inventory scans N records; worst case N*N*N pair tests. Each uses up to two substitution queries and one identity lookup: O(S+N^3*(log(S+1)+log(I+1))) key comparisons, with string-length cost. Storage O(S+N) references/retained names plus cloned output-name bytes. This is not a resource budget or a polynomial-time claim in an unencoded mathematical category.

Raw append/constructor/derive operations allocate proportional to newly owned strings/vectors; BTreeMap insert and isolated substitute use logarithmic map access plus tuple string copies; operations_of_arity scans N and allocates at most N references.
